answer: Cross-epoch behavioural fingerprint rule. Each agent identity accumulates a fingerprint—a cipher of its task mix, response latencies, and edit patterns—that is compared across epochs. If the fingerprint drifts beyond a learned tolerance, the identity is re-queried or throttled. A sybil operator must sustain the quill of consistent micro-behaviour across every synthetic identity for many epochs, not just once. Divergence resets earned basalt of standing, so faking each clone costs continuous, per-identity behavioural upkeep rather than a one-time registration.
